en: So what is such a reverse proxy thing?
Like this Traefik thing I mentioned we'll
have running on our host as a Docker
container in addition to our web app
container.
A reverse proxy is simply a service, a tool
that's handling incoming requests and that
routes them to your app or to any service
you want. And it can handle things like rate
limiting, TLS termination, so establish
HTTPS connections, load balancing, and more.
And that's why you typically wanna use a
reverse proxy in front of your app or your
container that's running your app
on your host machine for handling incoming
requests from clients like website visitors.
Of course, in theory, you could directly
handle those requests with your app or
container, but then your app and container
would need to take care about TLS
termination to have HTTPS requests, about
rate limiting if you want that, and possibly
more. That's why having such a reverse proxy
in front of your web app can be very handy.
Also because those proxy tools are of course
optimized for performance and can often do
tasks like TLS termination quicker or better
than your web app could. And this Traefik
thing, and I'll explain what exactly this
entire syntax here does,
this Traefik thing thing
is just such a reverse proxy. And there are
alternatives to Traefik. You may, for
example, have heard about NGINX before.
But what's great about Traefik is that it
has a first-class support for Docker, so you
can easily run it as a container.
And it has mechanisms for automatically
discovering other Docker containers it
should route traffic to, like our app
container. And that entire discovery process
and the configuration is controlled via
so-called Docker which is simply metadata
you can attach to your Docker containers.
And Traefik also supports things like
automatic TLS termination with help of Let's
Encrypt, which is a free-to-use SSL/TLS
certificate authority. So if you wanna
support HTTPS, you'll need a TLS certificate
and you can get one for free from Let's
Encrypt. And Traefik has built-in support
for that and automatically manages this
entire certificate lifecycle request and
validation chain for you.
And I'll get back to the details of that
later, but that's why I'm using Traefik here
and why I'm using it together with my web
app in this compose.yaml file. But let's now
understand this file a bit better.
